title: I'm Still Here
filmVersion: 2024 feature identified by title, year and director in ShotDeck. Transfer or edition not specified.
altText: Eunice, seen from behind, photographs her family and friends gathered on a sunny Rio beach.
rationale: The warm group composition makes the family's shared life visible. Eunice taking the photograph also connects naturally with the entry's concern for memory. It includes Rubens and the wider social circle without showing detention or a late outcome. This is an editorial selection, not a claim that audiences universally consider it the film's defining image.

title: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
filmVersion: 2004 feature identified by title, year and director in ShotDeck. Transfer or edition not specified.
altText: Joel and Clementine lie close together on blue-gray lake ice, viewed from directly above.
rationale: The overhead composition is visually distinctive and keeps both people together within the frozen lake's open space. It presents the tenderness the entry explains Joel later wants to preserve. The early frame gives the relationship visual priority without exposing the ending. Keep the surrounding ice; a tight face crop would lose the composition.

title: Soul
filmVersion: 2020 Pixar animated feature identified by title and year in ShotDeck. Transfer or edition not specified. ShotDeck displays Pete Docter; the co-director credit is retained from the existing researched batch record.
altText: Joe Gardner crosses a sunlit New York street while talking on the phone, carrying a briefcase.
rationale: Joe's long stride gives the frame energy, while autumn trees, sunlight and everyday traffic give the city a strong presence. This introduces the human world whose ordinary experiences matter to the entry. The frame comes early in the film and avoids showing a final decision or reducing the film to its imagined afterlife. Preserve the wide street view around Joe.
